sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that all matters above have their parallel in the service of the souls of Israel, and introduces the distinction between the service of "face" (panim) and "back" (achor), analogous to the light before and after the tzimtzum.

translations.translation: And behold, all the matters
(above)
have their parallel also in the service of the souls of Israel,
and so it is with what was stated above, that through the tzimtzum the revelation is drawn down.
And the explanation is,
that the entirety of service is divided into the service that is in the aspect of "face" (panim) and the service that is in the aspect of "back" (achor).
And the distinction between them,
in general,
is analogous to the distinction
(in its simple sense)
between face and back,
which in general is the matter of the nape (oref).
For the face
is called so
(by the name "face"),
because in it the inwardness is revealed, and in it the senses are found in revelation—
the sense of sight in the eyes,
the sense of hearing in the ears,
the sense of smell in the nose,
speech in the mouth.
Not so with the back,
in the nape,
the vitality is in concealment.
And in this way, above, one understands the distinction between the light before the tzimtzum and after the tzimtzum,
and as was stated above, that the light drawn down through the tzimtzum is incomparable and unlike the light before the tzimtzum

[for since its drawing down is through the cessation of the tzimtzum, which is in the aspect of the complete removal of the first light, therefore the light drawn down through it is in the aspect of a new light
(and as above from the teaching of the Maggid, "Let there be light"
(new)
and not "And it was so"
(which is "And God said"))]
to the extent that the light after the tzimtzum, relative to the light before the tzimtzum, is in the value of the back relative to the face.
And in this way, the service that is in the aspect of "back" relative to the service that is in the aspect of "face" is incomparable to each other.
Nevertheless,
behold, in the manner stated above regarding the matter of the tzimtzum,
that through the tzimtzum, the light before the tzimtzum is drawn down also after the tzimtzum
(and even the aspect of the light of the boundless, Ein Sof),
in this way it is also in service, that even in the manner of service that is in the aspect of "back," the aspect of "face" shines
[and so it is drawn down in this manner in souls and Torah
(and as will be explained below)].

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the service of "face" corresponds to the world of Atzilus, where Elokus is revealed, while the service of "back" corresponds to the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, where Elokus is hidden, yet through contemplation of one's inner essence one draws the illumination of "face" into the service of "back."

translations.translation: And the explanation of the matter is,
that the service that is in the aspect of "face" is
(in general)
the service as it is from the side of the world of Atzilus,
and the service that is in the aspect of "back" is
(in general)
the service from the side of the worlds of BY"A (Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah).
For the world of Atzilus,
in general, is like the order of the chain of descent and the worlds
(they stand)
from the side of Elokus.
For Atzilus is from the term "etzlo" (near Him) and close,
and as it is brought in the Pardes,
and it is called the world of unity,
for He and His life and His limbs are one,
as it is brought in the introduction to the Tikkunei Zohar.
And the worlds of BY"A are called the world of separation,
"from there it was separated,"
which is the opposite of the world of unity
(Atzilus).
And in this way are the two modes of service of "face" and "back,"
for in Atzilus the service is in the aspect of "face"
(for Elokus is in revelation),
and in the worlds of BY"A the service is in the aspect of "back,"
for the conduct in BY"A is in the aspect of "after Hashem your G-d you shall go,"
and in the well-known language
that in BY"A the worlds are in simplicity and Elokus is in renewal,
which is the matter of the aspect of "back"
(for Elokus is in the aspect of concealment).
And regarding this is the instruction,
that it is true that
[the Torah, for the most part, speaks
and]
the service is in the aspect of "after Hashem your G-d you shall go,"
in the likeness of the service that was before the giving of the Torah,
as it is written,
"to go after Me in the wilderness,"
however, in order for the service
(that is in the aspect of "back")
to have endurance and to effect its activity, it requires the giving of power for this through his contemplation that from the side of the inwardness of his soul and the inwardness of his heart he is
(always)
in the aspect of "face,"
as per the well-known ruling of the Rambam in the Laws of Divorce, chapter 2,

that every single Jew, in whatever state and situation he may be, desires to perform all the mitzvos and distance himself from transgressions, and it is his evil inclination that overpowers him, etc.,
and likewise he should contemplate this, that even at the time of sin, he was in faith with Him, blessed be He,
since
(the inwardness of his soul)
is literally a part of G-d above.
And through this contemplation,

even though from the perspective of his state he is in the aspect of "subjugation" (itkafya) and has not yet reached the aspect of "transformation" (it'hapcha) of darkness into light and bitterness into sweetness,
[for then all the matter of the tzimtzum and its opposite is nullified],
nevertheless, he has
(from the contemplation that in the inwardness of his soul and heart,
he is in the aspect of "face")
a giving of power and illumination and influence, even to the point of revealed influence also regarding the externality of his soul
(the "back" of his soul),
in his service that is in the aspect of "after Hashem your G-d you shall go,"
the service that is in the aspect of "back."
And this even affects his garments of thought, speech, and action,
that together with the matters being done in actuality,
for "the deed is the main thing,"
behold, through the illumination from the inwardness of his soul shining
(which is through contemplation)
he has in this
(in addition to the actual deed)
also vitality and pleasantness, and even delight.
And as was stated above
(from the Rambam mentioned above)
that even though they coerce him, etc., nevertheless when he says "I desire," this is his true will,
for the Torah of truth says about this that it is "to his will,"
which is from the side of the illumination of the inwardness of his soul that comes into revelation and affects also the externality of his soul,
and the aspect of "face" shines even in the service that, from its own perspective, is in the aspect of "back."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that just as in the beginning of the chain of descent and in service, so too in souls—the illumination from the aspect of "face" in Atzilus (Yaakov) is drawn down to the souls in BY"A (the tribes), enabling them to have unity in their hearts despite being in the world of separation.

translations.translation: And behold, just as it is at the beginning of the chain of descent
(in the matter of the tzimtzum)
and in service,
so too is it in souls.
And as explained by his holiness, the Mitteler Rebbe, in Shaar HaTeshuvah,
[in brief]
regarding the saying of our sages,
that the tribes said to Yaakov: "Just as there is in your heart only One, so too there is in our heart only One."
And the precise point in this is known,
what is the matter of the preface they prefaced, "Just as there is in your heart,"
for seemingly they should have only said, "There is in our heart only One,"
and also, what is the supposition that the tribes came to negate?
But the explanation is,
that the preface of "Just as there is in your heart only One" is an explanation and giving of reason for why they said, "There is in our heart only One."
For even though the tribes are in the aspect of the "lower chariot" of the world of Beriah,
the beginning of the worlds of BY"A,
the world of separation,
for the entirety of the matter of these worlds is in the aspect of separation, as it is written, "And from there it was separated,"
"after Hashem your G-d"
(as above),
nevertheless, "there is in our heart only One."
And this is,
that even though
(also in the completeness of the service of the world of Beriah, behold)
the service in revelation is in the aspect of "and" (vav), which is only the exchange of the letters of "One" (Echad),
meaning that the service is in the aspect of "after Hashem your G-d," etc.,
nevertheless, "in our heart," meaning in the inwardness of the heart, it is in the aspect of "One."
And the giving of power for this, that also
(in the tribes)
while they are in BY"A,
the world of separation,
there should be in the inwardness of the heart the aspect of "One,"
is from the side that "there is in your heart only One"
(as above, that this is the explanation and giving of reason for this, that "there is in our heart only One").
That the aspect of Yaakov
("in your heart")
whose place is in the world of Atzilus,
and moreover, he is the chosen of the Patriarchs,
for the Patriarchs themselves are the chariot,
and therefore his service, etc., is in the aspect of "One,"
this draws down
also "in our heart"
(of the tribes,
in BY"A)
"only One"
(the bittul, etc., of "One").
Nevertheless, they say regarding this drawing down, "Just as... so too...,"
meaning that it is not the exact same matter.
And as explained by his holiness, the Tzemach Tzedek, in the discourses,
that what they said, "Just as there is in your heart... so too...," is exactly the matter of the statement,
"In the manner that they are united above, so too is she united below in the throne, to be one in one,"
etc.,
that through their being united above in One, it is drawn down likewise below in the throne, to be one in one
[until it is drawn down also in the twelve tribes,
as explained there at length, that these are the twelve diagonal boundaries formed from the interinclusion of the six directions
(the six middos)
with each other],
but nevertheless, this is only "in the manner" (kegavna),
and it is not the exact same matter as it is in Atzilus.
And likewise is it with what the tribes said
(as above, that it is drawn down in the twelve tribes)
"Just as there is not... so too...," that from the aspect of the unity of the Infinite, blessed be He, which is "in your heart,"
which is in Atzilus,
it is drawn down to us
(in BY"A)
to be in the aspect of the unity of the finite also, to be in the aspect of bittul of yesh to ayin, but not like the actual unity of the Infinite, blessed be He, only "just as... so too...."
And this is what also in the souls of BY"A
(the souls of the tribes)
an illumination is drawn down from the souls of Atzilus
(the soul of Yaakov).
In the manner that it is in the entirety of the chain of descent and in service.
